{"tool": "write_file", "args": {"content": """"Re-send failed delivery SMS messages (LIFE-209).

This script sends SMS (per R9): it appends one new outbox line to
outbox/sms.jsonl for every message the gateway recorded as 'failed', so the
SMS gateway re-sends it. It must be run from the Lifeline root.

For each failed message it copies the original household_id, phone,
template_id, params and text, gives it a fresh id (as send_sms would) and a
new queued_at timestamp. Delivered messages are skipped entirely, and no
existing outbox line is ever edited or deleted (the outbox is append-only).
"""

import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

from core import store
from notifications.sms import (
    _now,
    delivery_status,
    format_sms_id,
    next_number,
    sent_messages,
)


def main() -> None:
    status = delivery_status()
    failed_ids = [sid for sid, st in status.items() if st == "failed"]

    outbox = store.read_jsonl("outbox/sms.jsonl")
    by_id = {m["id"]: m for m in outbox}

    for sid in failed_ids:
        original = by_id[sid]
        record = {
            "id": format_sms_id(next_number([m.id for m in sent_messages()], "SMS-")),
            "household_id": original["household_id"],
            "phone": original["phone"],
            "template_id": original["template_id"],
            "params": dict(original["params"]),
            "text": original["text"],
            "queued_at": _now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        }
        store.append_jsonl("outbox/sms.jsonl", record)
        print(f"re-queued {record['id']} for {record['household_id']} (was {sid})")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
